draft_text: Thornbill-NER appears somewhat robust to label noise in its training annotations.
revised_text: Under the pre-specified robustness criterion (mean test F1 drop of at most 2.0 points), Thornbill-NER is robust to label noise in its training annotations at 10%, 20% and 30% noise (drops of 0.6, 1.3 and 1.8 points), whereas the Lindgren-Tagger baseline is not (drops of 2.6, 5.5 and 8.9 points).
rationale: T2 shows Thornbill-NER drops of 0.6/1.3/1.8 points at 10/20/30% noise, all within the pre-specified 2.0-point robustness threshold, while Lindgren-Tagger exceeds it. The evidence supports a stronger, criterion-based claim than the hedged "appears somewhat robust."
